dmp.title: AeroSense Data Management Plan
dmp.description: Worked example: open sensor data. All content is synthetic; the DOIs use DataCite's test prefix 10.5072 and resolve nowhere.

dataset.title: AeroSense sensor readings
dataset.description: Air-quality readings from twelve field stations, one row per station and minute.
data_quality_assurance: Readings outside the sensors' calibrated ranges are flagged, not removed.
dataset.preservation_statement: Kept for at least ten years after the project ends, in the repository named below.

dataset.title: AeroSense calibration log
dataset.description: Calibration runs for every sensor, with the reference instrument's readings.

guide.title: Practical Guide to the International Alignment of Research Data Management

answers.1a: New data are collected by twelve field stations running the project's logging software; no existing data are re-used. Provenance is recorded per reading: station, sensor serial number and firmware version.
answers.1b: Numeric time series in CSV, about 5 GB over the project, and a calibration log in JSON. CSV is chosen because every analysis tool reads it and the repository lists it as a preferred format.
answers.2a: Each deposit carries DataCite metadata and a README describing columns, units and station locations. Files are named by station and month.
answers.2b: Readings outside the calibrated range of a sensor are flagged in a quality column; sensors are recalibrated every three months against a reference instrument.
answers.3a: During the project the data are kept on the institution's managed research storage, which is backed up nightly to a second site.
answers.3b: The data hold no personal or sensitive information. Write access is limited to the project team.
answers.4b: The data are owned by the project's institution and released under CC BY 4.0 (the readings) and CC0 (the calibration log). No third-party data are used.
answers.4c: No ethical issues are expected; the stations measure air on public land with the owners' permission.
answers.5a: Both datasets are deposited openly in Zenodo at the end of the second project year, without embargo.
answers.5b: All readings and the full calibration log are kept, since they cannot be measured again. Zenodo preserves them for the lifetime of the repository.
answers.5c: Any tool that reads CSV and JSON; the README names none in particular.
answers.5d: Zenodo assigns a DOI to each deposit; the DOIs are reserved in advance and recorded in this plan.
answers.6a: The project's data steward is responsible for carrying out and updating this plan, with the principal investigator.
answers.6b: Deposit in Zenodo is free; about two weeks of the data steward's time is budgeted for preparing the deposits.
